summary.text: Jo Anne Simon is the incumbent Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for NY State Assembly District 52 (parts of Brooklyn Heights, Downtown Brooklyn, Boerum Hill and nearby neighborhoods). A disability civil rights attorney and longtime Brooklyn civic and party figure, she was first elected in 2014 and took office in January 2015; she chairs the Assembly's Mental Health Committee and is a member of the Higher Education, Judiciary, Transportation and Ways and Means committees.

paragraphs.text: Grew up in a working-class neighborhood in Yonkers, NY, the oldest girl in a family of five and the daughter of Italian immigrants; was the first in her family to attend college.

Earned a bachelor's degree in Communication Sciences from Iona College, a master's degree in Education of the Deaf from Gallaudet University, and a law degree from Fordham University School of Law, completed at night while working full-time.

Worked as a judicial law secretary and taught in Hofstra University School of Law's clinical program before establishing a disability civil rights law firm in Downtown Brooklyn; is also an adjunct assistant professor of law at Fordham and general counsel of the Association on Higher Education And Disability (AHEAD).

Has lived in Brooklyn since 1981. Served as President of the Boerum Hill Association and was a founder or co-founder of several Brooklyn civic organizations, including the Downtown Brooklyn Coalition, BrooklynSpeaks.net and the Council of Brooklyn Neighborhoods; also chaired the Gowanus Community Stakeholder Group.

Elected female District Leader and State Committeewoman for the 52nd Assembly District in 2004, according to her official biography; the Brooklyn Paper reported in 2014 that she had served as female district leader since 2004.
Ran for New York City Council in 2009, according to the Brooklyn Paper, which reported that she and Doug Biviano lost that Council race to Steve Levin.

Won the 2014 Democratic primary for the open Assembly seat of retiring Assembly Member Joan Millman, defeating Peter Sikora and Doug Biviano, and then the general election; took office January 1, 2015.

Ballotpedia lists her as a candidate in the 2021 Democratic primary for Brooklyn Borough President and the 2022 Democratic primary for U.S. House in New York's 10th District; she did not win either primary and remained in the Assembly.

Current committee roles per the Assembly website: chair of the Committee on Mental Health and member of the Higher Education, Judiciary, Transportation and Ways and Means committees. Her official biography describes her as a member of the ARISE Coalition, which seeks to improve outcomes for New York City children with disabilities.
